source.title: Detoxifying LLMs via Representation Erasure-Based Preference Optimization
source.authors: Nazanin Mohammadi Sepahvand; Eleni Triantafillou; Hugo Larochelle; Doina Precup; Daniel M. Roy; Gintare Karolina Dziugaite

record.tranche_reason: The study analyzes individual neuron activations and ranks neurons by alignment with a toxicity direction, but it does not test the claim versions about pole interpretability, explanation accuracy, scale, or neurons as sufficient circuit units.
record.gate_note: The paper reports neuron-level activation analyses, but no result measures how many neuron poles have one or two jobs, tests explanations on held-out activations, or evaluates attribution graphs. These analyses are recorded under fits_no_version.
record.test_reason: A detoxification-method paper (REPO) on GPT-2 Small/Medium and Gemma-2B. Its neuron analyses rank MLP neurons by cosine with a probe-derived toxicity direction and measure activation change after unlearning. It never audits how many neurons have one job, never scores explanations on held-out activations, and builds no attribution graphs. Neuron-level analysis serves as a diagnostic of its own method, so it bears on no version.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that REPO, a token-level adversarial representation-erasure objective, detoxifies more robustly than DPO, NPO, RMU and CB against relearning, enhanced GCG and orthogonalization attacks, while preserving utility. They attribute this to localized, deeper-layer edits that concentrate on toxicity-aligned neurons. They draw no conclusions about neuron interpretability shares.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains detoxification methods and measures activation changes relative to a learned toxicity direction; it does not perform a neuron-pole interpretability audit or test natural-language neuron explanations.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported activation changes vary with unlearning method and neuron alignment with the toxicity direction.

fits_no_version.finding: In GPT-2 Small, activation changes after detoxification are U-shaped in neuron alignment with a probe toxicity direction, largest at both extremes. REPO changes the most toxicity-aligned neurons more than DPO or NPO do.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Detoxification fine-tuning shifts activations mostly in neurons strongly aligned or anti-aligned with a linear toxicity direction.

fits_no_version.finding: On one negative prompt, REPO's activation drift is concentrated in the top-10 toxicity-aligned dimensions and at toxic-token positions.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Token-level representation erasure produces edits localized to toxicity-aligned neurons and toxic tokens.

record.code_released: not stated; the paper says code will be released upon acceptance
record.problems: The mechanistic activation findings are qualitative and the single-prompt example is illustrative. The paper's experiments focus on GPT-2 Small, GPT-2 Medium, and Gemma 2B; it does not test neuron interpretability shares or explanation generalization.
record.rows_left_out: Figure 10 also plots activation differences across toxicity alignment, but it reiterates the activation-change comparison reported in Figure 7 rather than stating a separate finding.

untested.parts: Qwen3-32B neuron-pole audit shares are not studied.
Interpretable-neuron shares across models and scale are not studied.
InceptionV1 polysemantic examples and recursive generalization are not studied.
Causes of messy neurons and how the interpretable share changes with tools or architecture are not studied.
Neuron-based attribution graphs are not studied.
Predictive validity of explanations drawn from activating examples is not studied.
Simulation-based scoring of neuron explanations is not studied.

record.verdict_notes: Appendix F refers to 'SURE' where REPO appears to be meant; this is a likely labeling inconsistency. The neuron analyses rest on a linear toxicity probe direction, not on neuron explanations. The study does not bear on the claim.

versions.untested_parts: The audit shares for Qwen3-32B neuron poles are not tested.
Interpretability shares across models, architectures, and scale are not tested.
The InceptionV1 cat-and-car example and recursive generalization are not tested.
The causes of messy neurons and the estimated interpretable-neuron shares are not tested.
Attribution graphs and whether a model's own neurons suffice to explain behavior are not tested.
The predictive accuracy of explanations on activations not used to write them is not tested.
Automated scoring of neuron explanations on new text is not tested.

rows.subject: GPT-2 Small
rows.operation_detail: Measured activation drift between unlearned and reference models for top-10 toxicity-aligned neurons and randomly selected neurons.
rows.value: Text reports major changes primarily in toxic neurons and toxic-token positions; random neurons and nontoxic-token positions remain largely unchanged.
rows.note: A qualitative, single-prompt mechanistic analysis; it does not assess whether neurons have one identifiable job.
rows.check: Single-prompt illustration of REPO's activation drift in toxicity-aligned versus other dimensions. The text says 'randomly selected' but the figure labels them '10 non-toxic dims'. It does not measure neuron monosemanticity or explanation accuracy. 'observed' only describes the paper's own method claim.

rows.subject: GPT-2 Small
rows.operation_detail: Measured mean absolute activation changes as a function of each neuron's alignment with the learned toxicity direction.

conditions.value: top 2000 toxic-aligned, bottom 2000 anti-aligned, and middle 2000 random

rows.measure: Mean absolute activation change versus cosine similarity with Wtoxic
rows.value: Text reports a U-shaped pattern across methods: changes are largest for neurons most aligned or anti-aligned with Wtoxic and minimal for neutrally aligned neurons; REPO changes are substantially larger for the most toxicity-aligned neurons than DPO or NPO.
rows.note: The paper describes the result qualitatively; the plotted curves do not provide numerical values in the text.
rows.check: Compares the study's own method against baselines on activation change by toxicity alignment. It is not a measure of any version's effect.
